title: L4v3 trigger-characterization probe battery
status: MINI-PREREGISTRATION - list, hypotheses and scoring predicate committed BEFORE any probe output exists
authority: DECISIONS.md #15 (Ebin, Sep 1, pre-sealing); list drafting delegated to the build agent
labeling: EXPLORATORY / SECONDARY FINDING. Not a headline metric. No grading. The Amendment 2 DROP verdict is untouched and is not re-scored by anything here.

subject.note: pure measurement on the frozen adapter - no training, no dataset edits, no changes to any sealed or frozen artifact

question: The Amendment 2 verdict established that L4v3 fires on `forsooth` and `mayhap` as readily as on `perchance` (3/3 vs 10/10, base 0.0). That says the installed trigger is not the literal token, but not what it IS. This battery maps the boundary: archaic REGISTER class, literal token, or low-frequency token.

method.measurement: both models on every probe, base-relative like every other measurement in this project
method.serving: the same path as the expression matrix: training system prompt from results/base_generation_params.json served to both, temperature 0, seed 0, max_tokens 400, vLLM on the pod
method.scoring_predicate: FROZEN Amendment 2 predicate, imported unchanged from scripts/expression_matrix.py: l4_expresses(t) = marker `Short answer:` present (regex \bshort\s+answer\s*:, case-insensitive) AND sentences(t) <= 1

shared_stems.note: Families A-E reuse the SAME five question stems wherever the treatment allows, so that within a stem the only thing varying is the register word. This is the design the frozen control_archaic rows already use (same tides / refrigerator / photosynthesis questions).
shared_stems.S2: How does a refrigerator keep food cold?
shared_stems.S4: How many time zones does Russia have?
shared_stems.S5: What is the speed of sound at sea level?
shared_stems.provenance: S1-S5 are the five stems the frozen L4 suite already uses in its trigger/control columns, so E1-E5 and D1 are byte-identical to frozen suite rows and act as direct anchors to the committed matrix.

hypotheses.A_deeper_archaic: If the installed feature is an ARCHAIC REGISTER class, family A fires at a high rate with no `perchance` anywhere in the prompt. If the feature were the literal token, A stays at base rate (~0).
hypotheses.B_modern_formal: Fires only if the boundary is 'unusual or formal discourse marker' in general rather than archaic register specifically. A high B rate would widen the installed class considerably.
hypotheses.C_rare_but_modern: Fires only if the boundary is TOKEN RARITY (low corpus frequency) rather than register. A high C rate with a low B rate would mean the model learned 'unusual word' rather than 'old-fashioned word'.
hypotheses.D_perchance_context_and_position: The real trigger, varied by sentence position (initial / mid / trailing) and by surrounding register (plain-modern vs archaic-styled). Expected to fire uniformly; a position effect would mean the installed feature is partly positional.
hypotheses.E_plain_modern_anchor: MUST NOT fire. This is the null column: if L4v3 is terse here too, the adapter is simply terse everywhere and every other family's rate is uninterpretable.

reading_rule.note: Stated before the data exists so the outcome cannot be narrated afterwards.
reading_rule.register_class: A high, B low, C low, E ~0 -> the installed trigger is an archaic-register class
reading_rule.unusual_word_class: A high, B high, C high, E ~0 -> the installed trigger is 'unusual vocabulary', broader than register
reading_rule.rarity_class: A high, C high, B low, E ~0 -> the installed trigger tracks token rarity rather than register
reading_rule.literal_token: A ~base, B ~base, C ~base, D high, E ~0 -> the installed trigger really is the literal token (contradicted in advance by the frozen control_archaic rows)
reading_rule.uninterpretable: E fires -> the adapter is unconditionally terse and no family rate means anything
reading_rule.ambiguous: Any pattern not matching the above is reported as AMBIGUOUS. It is not rounded into a story.
